topic: Strange borders countdown: Valga-Valka to India's enclaves
hook: Your walk across one small town takes you from Estonia to Latvia, and India has a border stranger still.
title: 6 Borders That Make No Sense, Ending in India
description: A walk across one small town takes you from Estonia to Latvia, and that is only number six. Count down six real borders that make no sense, from Valga-Valka and a German town inside Switzerland to the tangle of enclaves on the India-Bangladesh border. Every place is real and on the map.

scenes.narration: Your walk across one small town takes you from Estonia to Latvia, and India has a border stranger still.
scenes.headline: One Town, Two Countries

scenes.narration: By the end, you will see a patch of Indian land inside Bangladeshi land, inside Indian land, inside Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: Land Inside Land

scenes.narration: Six real borders. Each one stranger than the last. And number one is right here in India.
scenes.headline: Six Real Borders

scenes.narration: We start with a town where the border runs down a street, through a square and across a park.
scenes.headline: Street, Square, Park

scenes.narration: Stay for the last one. Many people have never heard of it, and it only disappeared from the map in 2015.
scenes.headline: Gone In 2015

scenes.narration: So let's start the countdown at number six, in a small town in the Baltics.
scenes.headline: Countdown Starts

scenes.narration: Number six. One town, two countries, and you can cross the border on your way to the shop.
scenes.headline: 6. Valga-Valka

scenes.narration: It is called Valga on the Estonian side and Valka on the Latvian side. Same town, two names, two countries.
scenes.headline: Two Names, One Town

scenes.narration: Look at the map and you see one built-up town, with a border line cutting straight through the middle.
scenes.headline: A Line Through Town

scenes.narration: The border runs along a street, across a square and through a park. You can step over it without noticing.
scenes.headline: Step Over It

scenes.narration: Each half has its own town council, its own flag and its own local rules, yet the buildings sit side by side.
scenes.headline: Two Councils

scenes.narration: So how did this happen? In 1920, both Estonia and Latvia claimed the town, and neither would give way.
scenes.headline: Both Wanted It

scenes.narration: A British officer, Colonel Tallents, was asked to settle it. He drew a line that split the town in two.
scenes.headline: A Line Drawn

scenes.narration: For decades that hardly mattered, because both countries were inside the Soviet Union and the border was only on paper.
scenes.headline: A Paper Border

scenes.narration: Then the Soviet Union ended, and that paper line became a real border between two independent countries again.
scenes.headline: A Real Border Again

scenes.narration: Today both countries are in the Schengen area, so you can walk across with no passport check at all.
scenes.headline: No Passport Check

scenes.narration: Both even use the euro. But during Covid, checks came back for a while, and the town felt cut in half.
scenes.headline: Covid Checks

scenes.narration: Estonian is spoken on one side and Latvian on the other, yet people move between them like crossing a road.
scenes.headline: Two Languages

scenes.narration: A town split in half is strange. But wait until you see a town that is stuck inside another country.
scenes.headline: It Gets Stranger

scenes.narration: Number five. There is a town that is German on paper, yet completely surrounded by Switzerland on every side.
scenes.headline: 5. Büsingen

scenes.narration: It is called Büsingen. Look at the map and you see a small German pocket sitting inside the Swiss border.
scenes.headline: A German Pocket

scenes.narration: The town is part of the Swiss customs area, even though it belongs to Germany.
scenes.headline: Swiss Customs Zone

scenes.narration: Shops accept Swiss francs, and many people use them every day, even though the town is in Germany.
scenes.headline: Swiss Francs Used

scenes.narration: Its cars carry a special German number plate with the letters BÜS, so you can spot a Büsingen car at once.
scenes.headline: The BÜS Plate

scenes.narration: Its laws are mostly German, but many everyday habits feel Swiss, because Switzerland is all around it.
scenes.headline: German Laws, Swiss Life

scenes.narration: Old land deals and treaties from centuries ago left the town cut off, and nobody ever fixed it.
scenes.headline: Old Deals, Odd Map

scenes.narration: A German town inside Switzerland is odd. Next is a Spanish town stuck inside France.
scenes.headline: Next: Spain In France

scenes.narration: Number four. Llívia is a Spanish town, but you can only reach it by driving through France.
scenes.headline: 4. Llívia

scenes.narration: It sits in a valley in the Pyrenees mountains, with French land on every side.
scenes.headline: Ringed By France

scenes.narration: In 1659 Spain and France signed a treaty, and Spain handed over a set of villages to France.
scenes.headline: The 1659 Treaty

scenes.narration: Llívia was officially a town, not a village. So the treaty did not count it, and it stayed Spanish.
scenes.headline: Town, Not Village

scenes.narration: That tiny technical difference is why a Spanish town sits inside France today, more than three hundred years later.
scenes.headline: A Tiny Technicality

scenes.narration: A road links it back to Spain through French land, so you cross a border just to reach a Spanish town.
scenes.headline: Road Through France

scenes.narration: Llívia is quiet and peaceful. Next is a place where a mapmaker's mistake left American land cut off by Canada.
scenes.headline: A Mapmaker's Mistake

scenes.narration: Number three. There is a piece of the United States that you can only reach by land if you pass through Canada.
scenes.headline: 3. Northwest Angle
scenes.sub: US land cut off by Canada

scenes.narration: It is called the Northwest Angle, a small piece of Minnesota that sticks up into a huge lake called Lake of the Woods.
scenes.headline: Minnesota's Odd Corner

scenes.narration: To get there by road, you drive through Canada and then take a boat across the water to American land.
scenes.headline: Through Canada, By Boat

scenes.narration: In winter the lake freezes and an ice road opens, so you can drive on frozen water to reach the United States.
scenes.headline: An Ice Road

scenes.narration: Only a small number of people live there, and fishing lodges are a big part of life on the Angle.
scenes.headline: Fishing Lodges

scenes.narration: Why does it exist? An old treaty from 1783 was written using a map with mistakes on it.
scenes.headline: A Faulty Map

scenes.narration: The mapmakers did not know the real shape of the land, so the line the treaty described did not fit it.
scenes.headline: The Line Did Not Fit

scenes.narration: Later talks tried to fix the line, but they left this odd corner on the American side.
scenes.headline: Fixed, But Not Here

scenes.narration: So the Angle is American, but cut off from the rest of its country by a lake and by Canada.
scenes.headline: Cut Off By A Lake

scenes.narration: If you enjoy strange places like these, subscribe, because there are more coming, and a few are even stranger.
scenes.headline: More Strange Places

scenes.narration: Number two is not a small pocket. It is a whole region of a huge country, sitting far away from it.
scenes.headline: A Whole Region

scenes.narration: Number two. Russia owns a piece of land in Europe that does not touch the rest of Russia.
scenes.headline: 2. Kaliningrad

scenes.narration: It is called Kaliningrad, and it sits on the Baltic Sea, between Poland and Lithuania.
scenes.headline: Between Poland, Lithuania

scenes.narration: The land was once German, and its main city was Königsberg. After the Second World War, it became Russian.
scenes.headline: Once Königsberg

scenes.narration: Later the Soviet Union ended, the countries around it became independent, and Kaliningrad was cut off from Russia by land.
scenes.headline: Cut Off By Land

scenes.narration: To go from Moscow to Kaliningrad by land, you must cross other countries. Many travellers fly or go by sea.
scenes.headline: Fly Or Sail

scenes.narration: Imagine a piece of India that you could only reach through another country. That is how Kaliningrad works for Russia.
scenes.headline: Imagine It For India

scenes.narration: It is also home to a large Russian naval base on the Baltic Sea.
scenes.headline: A Naval Base

scenes.narration: Even so, it is a working region with ports, roads and a big city, all far from Moscow.
scenes.headline: Far From Moscow

scenes.narration: That is strange. But now we reach number one, and it is not in Europe or America. It is in India.
scenes.headline: Now, Number One

scenes.narration: Number one. India's strangest border was not a single line at all. It was a puzzle of tiny islands of land.
scenes.headline: 1. India's Enclaves

scenes.narration: Along the India-Bangladesh border, there were small patches of Indian land sitting inside Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: Indian Land In Bangladesh

scenes.narration: And there were patches of Bangladeshi land inside India. These patches are called enclaves.
scenes.headline: Bangladeshi Land In India

scenes.narration: There were 111 Indian enclaves inside Bangladesh, and 51 Bangladeshi enclaves inside India.
scenes.headline: 111 And 51

scenes.narration: The tangle goes back to old deals between the kings of Cooch Behar and the Mughals, long before 1947.
scenes.headline: Old Kings, Old Deals

scenes.narration: When India and Pakistan split in 1947, the new line was drawn around these patches, and the puzzle stayed.
scenes.headline: 1947 Left The Puzzle

scenes.narration: People in an enclave were stuck. To reach a school or a hospital, they often had to cross into the other country.
scenes.headline: Stuck In An Enclave

scenes.narration: Many lacked basic services, because neither country could easily reach them.
scenes.headline: Cut Off From Services

scenes.narration: In 2011, officials from both countries went door to door in the enclaves to count the people living there.
scenes.headline: A Joint Headcount

scenes.narration: Then there was the most extreme case, a place called Dahala Khagrabari, in the middle of the puzzle.
scenes.headline: Dahala Khagrabari

scenes.narration: It was a patch of Indian land inside Bangladeshi land, inside Indian land, inside Bangladesh. Land inside land inside land.
scenes.headline: Land In Land In Land

scenes.narration: Reports called it the only place of its kind in the world, a third-level enclave.
scenes.headline: One Of A Kind

scenes.narration: At midnight on 31 July 2015, India and Bangladesh finally swapped these lands under a land border agreement.
scenes.headline: Midnight, 2015

scenes.narration: Residents were allowed to choose which country they wanted to belong to, and some chose to move.
scenes.headline: Residents Chose

scenes.narration: Many people celebrated that night, and the tangle of enclaves was gone from the map.
scenes.headline: The Tangle Is Gone

scenes.narration: So the strangest border in India is one you can no longer visit. It now lives on old maps.
scenes.headline: Only On Old Maps

scenes.narration: A border made of tiny islands inside islands is stranger than any single line, and that is why it takes number one.
scenes.headline: Why It's Number One

scenes.narration: So here is the countdown again. Six, Valga and Valka, a town split between Estonia and Latvia.
scenes.headline: Six: Valga-Valka

scenes.narration: Five, a German town inside Switzerland. Four, a Spanish town inside France. Three, an American corner reached through Canada.
scenes.headline: Five, Four, Three

scenes.narration: Two, Russian land far from Russia. And one, India's tangle of land inside land inside land.
scenes.headline: Two And One

scenes.narration: Maps look neat and solid. But every line on them was drawn by people, and people make strange choices.
scenes.headline: People Drew These Lines

scenes.narration: Now think back to the start. Your walk across one small town takes you from Estonia to Latvia.
scenes.headline: Back To Valga-Valka

scenes.narration: Come back tomorrow for another place on the map that should not exist, and it is real.
scenes.headline: Tomorrow: Another Place
